observations.finding: Treated fields (4 fields) are sparse/isolated cells with large gaps vs DMSO control which is a near-confluent monolayer. Visible at identical contrast. Not covered by a provided z-score.
F-actin (red) in treated cells is markedly brighter with thick cortical ring and spiky filopodia-like projections at periphery, vs thin cortical actin in DMSO.
Beta-tubulin (green) is dimmer and diffuse with loss of filamentous radial microtubule network seen in DMSO; green signal faint in cytoplasm vs strong perinuclear and filamentous in control.
Overall color balance shifted to red-dominant (actin) over green (tubulin) in treated cells; DMSO shows balanced red cortex + bright green microtubules. Yellow overlap in rounded mitotic-like cells.
Actin texture is heterogeneous/patchy with high contrast spiky cortex vs smooth low-contrast actin in DMSO.

DNA (blue) frequently enlarged and irregular: multilobed, grape-like clusters of 3-10 small nuclei/micronuclei within a single cytoplasm (multinucleation/polyploidy) and enlarged irregular single nuclei, vs single round-oval uniform nuclei in DMSO. Frequent large cells with multiple micronuclei.

notable_cells.why: example cluster of ~8 micronuclei within one actin cortex
representative large multilobed nucleus vs DMSO single nucleus

candidate_mechanisms.why: Multinucleation / multilobed enlarged irregular nuclei with increased large-nucleus fraction and decreased solidity/form-factor is hallmark of Aurora B inhibition and cytokinesis failure/polyploidy. Secondary cortical actin prominence and reduced tubulin filament signal consistent with provided z-scores; not typical of pure Actin disruptors (which decrease organized F-actin) or pure Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers alone.

report.uncertainty: Only composite images available; no separate grayscale tubulin/actin/DNA channels to quantify filament loss. Microtubule destabilizers and DNA replication stress can also cause enlarged nuclei, but grape-like micronuclei clusters most specifically support Aurora.

data.note:
Note: Unblinded nocodazole (PubChem CID 4122, BBBC021 structure agree, ChEMBL CHEMBL9514 no curated mechanism) matches our conclusion Microtubule destabilizers (p=0.78) — scored correct by code.

Evidence: NSC 3/4 votes + 10/10 k-neighbors as microtubule destabilizers (e16), dose-dependent tubulin loss tub_mean rho -1.0 p=0 (e18), massive act_tub_ratio z +43.4/+32.3 at 3/1 µM (e2,e14) with visual loss of filamentous beta-tubulin and red-dominant actin, plus enlarged/multinucleated nuclei and large-nucleus fraction z up to 17.1.

Literature: PMID 14614453 explicitly titles nocodazole as "a microtubule destabilizer" triggering spindle checkpoint; consistent with our tubulin depolymerization + cytokinesis failure/multinucleation phenotype. PubChem/ChEMBL lookup confirms identity (e26).

Follow-up as proposed: tubulin-GFP washout + pHH3 assay vs reference destabilizer control to confirm depolymerization dynamics.

reflection.text:
Unblinding: nocodazole, CID 4122, T=Microtubule destabilizers, call=Microtubule destabilizers p=0.78 - CORRECT. Identity check e25/e26 name and BBBC021 structure agree, ChEMBL had no curated mechanism, so call rested entirely on phenotype.

What got it right:
Acquisition strategy covered the dynamic range usefully. e1 offered 0.001-3 uM with 4 wells. We sampled 3 uM (e2), 0.1 uM (e3), then filled 1 uM (e14) and 0.01 uM (e15). That gave a 0.01-3 uM dose series which discriminated onset vs collapse: e15 at 0.01 uM shows only weak actin changes z~+6.2 and no solidity collapse, e3 at 0.1 uM already shows nuc_solidity -24.2, act_mean +23.7, act_tub_ratio +20.1, e14 at 1 uM act_tub_ratio +32.3, nuc_solidity -30.4, and e2 at 3 uM act_tub_ratio +43.4, nuc_solidity -20.3, act_mean +19.2. This monotonic relative actin dominance and solidity loss tracked the unblinded compound identity, which literature in this run explicitly describes as nocodazole, a microtubule destabilizer PMID 14614453.

Comparison to reference atlas was decisive and consistent. e4 2/2 NSC and 10/10 k-neighbours for destabilizers, then e16 after 4 wells 3/4 NSC and 10/10 k-neighbours. That outweighed visual candidates.

Dose_response resolved the key discriminator: tub_mean rho=-1.00 p=0 over 4 wells (e18). Review critique notes the absolute values went from ~+1.8/+1.5 at 0.01/0.1 uM to ~-6.8/-9.1 at 1/3 uM, i.e. true tubulin loss, not just relative ratio inflation. Actin mean trend was weak rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e17), so high act_tub_ratio was driven by tubulin collapse - inconsistent with pure Actin disruptors which would not show progressive tub_mean loss. This correctly downweighted Actin disruptors to 0.08 and stabilizers/Eg5 to ~0.01/0.005 despite their shared large/multilobed nuclei signatures.

What misled and what we missed:
Microscopist descriptions were misleading in isolation: e5 on 4 fields suggested Aurora kinase inhibitors, e6 on 2 fields suggested Actin disruptors, both noting lower density vs DMSO. These reflect real overlapping features: frac_large_nucleus rose rho=+0.80 (e19), nuc_solidity was extremely low -20 to -30 in e2/e14, and frac_multinucleate_proxy was noted visually - all seen with Aurora inhibition and with microtubule destabilization leading to mitotic failure. We did not independently validate multinucleation or mitotic fraction dose trends initially: e7-e13 with only 2 wells returned 'Need at least 3 wells' for frac_large_nucleus, frac_mitotic_like, frac_multinucleate_proxy, nuc_solidity, tub_mean, act_mean, cell_count. Only after 4 wells could we test trends, and even then frac_large_nucleus, nuc_solidity, cell_count trends were non-significant (rho -0.40 p=0.6 e20, rho -0.20 p=0.8 e22, rho +0.40 p=0.6 e21). Cell_count did not show strong dose-dependent drop despite visual 'density lower' - quantitative count tempered the visual toxicity impression.

We also have only single replicates per dose and exhausted budget 0/4 left, so p=0 for tub_mean with n=4 is nominally strong but based on minimal sampling, and literature search for 'microtubule destabilizer multinucleation actin tubulin ratio phenotype' returned 0 hits (e28). No paper in this run directly validates the screening actin/tubulin ratio signature; PMID 14614453 only confirms the compound-class label. We missed an opportunity to acquire 0.03 uM and 0.001 uM to better define EC onset and to run a washout or tubulin-GFP time-lapse as proposed, which would have more directly proven depolymerization vs mitotic arrest. Within limits, 0.78 was appropriately calibrated rather than overconfident, retaining 0.12 Aurora and 0.08 Actin probability for the shared nuclear/actin components.

What misled and what we missed:
Microscopist descriptions were misleading in isolation: e5 on 4 fields suggested Aurora kinase inhibitors, e6 on 2 fields suggested Actin disruptors, both noting lower density vs DMSO. These reflect real overlapping features: frac_large_nucleus rose rho=+0.80 (e19), nuc_solidity was extremely low -20 to -30 in e2/e14, and frac_multinucleate_proxy was noted visually - all seen with Aurora inhibition and with microtubule destabilization leading to mitotic failure. We did not independently validate multinucleation or mitotic fraction dose trends initially: e7-e13 with only 2 wells returned 'Need at least 3 wells' for frac_large_nucleus, frac_mitotic_like, frac_multinucleate_proxy, nuc_solidity, tub_mean, act_mean, cell_count. Only after 4 wells could we test trends, and even then frac_large_nucleus, nuc_solidity, cell_count trends were non-significant (rho -0.40 p=0.6 e20, rho -0.20 p=0.8 e22, rho +0.40 p=0.6 e21). Cell_count did not show strong dose-dependent drop despite visual 'density lower' - quantitative count tempered the visual toxicity impression.

We also have only single replicates per dose and exhausted budget 0/4 left, so p=0 for tub_mean with n=4 is nominally strong but based on minimal sampling, and literature search for 'microtubule destabilizer multinucleation actin tubulin ratio phenotype' returned 0 hits (e28). No paper in this run directly validates the screening actin/tubulin ratio signature; PMID 14614453 only confirms the compound-class label. We missed an opportunity to acquire 0.03 uM and 0.001 uM to better define EC onset and to run a washout or tubulin-GFP time-lapse as proposed, which would have more directly proven depolymerization vs mitotic arrest. Within limits, 0.78 was appropriately calibrated rather than overconfident, retaining 0.12 Aurora and 0.08 Actin probability for the shared nuclear/actin components.

What was right:
- atlas NSC 3/4 and 10/10 neighbours for Microtubule destabilizers (e16) and monotonic tub_mean rho=-1.00 (e18)
- dose series 0.01/0.1/1/3 uM capturing threshold to collapse: act_tub_ratio +43.4 at 3uM e2, +32.3 at 1uM e14, +20.1 at 0.1uM e3, vs +6.2 at 0.01uM e15
- correct downweighting of Aurora (e5) and Actin (e6) visual candidates because they do not explain progressive tubulin loss

What was wrong or missed:
- visual phenotype candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors e5 and Actin disruptors e6 were misleading due to enlarged/multilobed low-solidity nuclei and high act_mean
- initial 2-well dose_response checks e7-e13 insufficient for trends; even with 4 wells most trends non-significant except tub_mean
- cell_count visual vs quantitative mismatch: density lower visually but rho -0.20 p=0.8 e22
- no curated ChEMBL mechanism e25/e26 and no literature hit for ratio phenotype e28, leaving atlas as sole external anchor

Proposed next experiment: live-cell tubulin-GFP washout 0.03-3 uM plus phospho-H3 to distinguish depolymerization from mitotic arrest, with replicate wells at 1 and 3 uM
